learning.title: A pull request reference is not a work item, and a policy field is read by a regex that a dash does not satisfy
learning.trigger: Filling a pull request body's owning-work-item field, or editing a verification checklist that another seat has already touched.
learning.rule: A ticket or owning-work-item field must name an ISSUE. The validator resolves the number against the live API and rejects any number that carries a `pull_request` field, so a PR number in that field fails even though the link resolves and reads correctly in a browser. The issue a PR served and the PR itself are different numbers: the PR body's own first line names the issue, and that is the number the field wants.

A policy field is matched by a regex, not read for meaning. The verification checklist accepts `N/A: reason` and rejects `N/A - reason`, because the pattern requires the colon. A one-character difference between two forms that a human reads identically decides whether the gate is green, so the form is copied from the validator rather than written from sense.

The body is a shared surface. Other seats tick boxes and rewrite lines, so a body that validated when its author wrote it can fail later without the author touching it. "The author validated it" and "the live body validates" are different claims, and only a check run against the live body answers the second. Re-run the live check after any edit, including edits made by someone else.

verification.requirement: Record the live check's own output (ok and errors) against the current head, not the exit code of the command that edited the body. A body validated only before another seat's edit is treated as unvalidated.
